key_insight: HalluScope adds fine-grained diagnosis for multimodal LLM hallucinations by jointly detecting errors, classifying their type, and generating explanations.
clinical_relevance: Better hallucination diagnosis could improve reliability of vision-language AI used in clinical workflows by making errors easier to identify, understand, and correct.
method: Built HalluScope-30K, a large diagnostic dataset with eight hallucination sources and five task categories.
Trained HalluScope-4B and HalluScope-8B using a multi-granular joint reward objective.
Evaluated both diagnosis performance and whether generated explanations could help other models correct hallucinations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports state-of-the-art results on the MHALO benchmark and a fine-grained classification benchmark, plus successful feedback-based correction on Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct and LLaVA-1.5-7B.
watch_item: The work is benchmark-driven, so real-world clinical usefulness may still depend on external validation in safety-critical settings.
paper_title: HalluScope: Fine-grained Hallucination Diagnosis for Multimodal Large Language Models
